The '''2019–20 Georgia State Panthers men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgia State University]] during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team's head coach was [[Rob Lanier]], who was coaching his first season at Georgia State. The Panthers played their home games at the [[GSU Sports Arena]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]] as a member of the [[Sun Belt Conference]]. They finished the season 19–13, 12–8 in Sun Belt play to finish in a tie for fourth place. They were the No. 4 seed in the [[2020 Sun Belt Conference men's basketball tournament|Sun Belt tournament]], where they lost to Georgia Southern.

== Previous season ==
The Panthers finished the season 24–10, 13–5 in the Sun Belt, claiming the title of SBC regular season champions. The Panthers also went on to defeat [[2018–19 Texas State Bobcats men's basketball team|Texas State]] and [[2018–19 UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball team|UT Arlington]] to become back-to-back champions of the [[2019 Sun Belt Conference men's basketball tournament|Sun Belt tournament]]. As a result, they received the Sun Belt's automatic bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 14 seed in the Midwest region, they lost to [[2018–19 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the first round.
After losing in the NCAA tournament, it was reported that head coach [[Ron Hunter]] had been offered the head coaching position at [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]], to which he responded that he was going to take 48 hours to think about the future.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bradley |first1=Mark |title=Ron Hunter says he's leaving Georgia State for Tulane |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/mark-bradley/ron-hunter-says-leaving-georgia-state-for-tulane/rk8itjdP8fg6bWNcoZQ39H/ |website=AJC.com |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref> On March 24, Tulane officially announced Hunter as head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tulane Names Ron Hunter Men's Basketball Head Coach |url=https://tulanegreenwave.com/news/2019/3/24/tulane-names-ron-hunter-mens-basketball-head-coach.aspx |website=TulaneGreenWave.com |publisher=Tulane Athletics |accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref> It was later reported Hunter opted to leave Georgia State due to a disagreement between the university and Hunter over contract details regarding performance bonuses, tying them to his team's GPA, which was purported by the university to be declining year after year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roberson |first1=Doug |title=What went wrong between Ron Hunter and Georgia State |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/what-went-wrong-between-ron-hunter-and-georgia-state/zOpfP2Y9sxOj8bh9QdYNlL/ |website=AJC.com |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref> On 5 April 2019, Georgia State announced the selection of Rob Lanier, associate head coach for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Vols]], to head the program at GSU.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vivlamore |first1=Chris |title=Georgia State hires Rob Lanier as men's basketball coach |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/georgia-state-hires-rob-lanier-men-basketball-coach/rS1pyme0JGcfKwoPivRfaP/ |website=AJC.com |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref>
